items.title: Universal injectivity of a module map is equivalent to the functor C giving a split surjection
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring R and a morphism f: M to N of modules, the lemma shows that f is universally injective exactly when the induced map C(N) to C(M) is a split surjection (statement lines 1218-1222). The proof uses the adjunction identity to replace the induced map on Hom groups by the base changed map inside C, exhibiting a commutative square whose vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 1224-1233). The forward direction then reads surjectivity of the rows at P equal to C(M), which lets the identity of C(M) be lifted to a splitting of C(f); the converse uses surjectivity of the rows for arbitrary P together with faithfulness of C to conclude that every base change of f is injective (proof lines 1234-1242). The claim is H2: a short but complete argument whose content is the correct choice of the test object P and the two one-line transfers.
